scenarios: a loaded extension's before_tool handler rewrites a write; unloading removes it
an extension unloaded while its slow handler runs has the rewrite discarded (UNLOADED) and the call writes what was asked
refusals by name for a missing directory, manifest, invalid manifest, duplicate load and unknown unload
after a restart a loaded extension is in force and an unloaded one is not
audit: NOT-FOUND before: no extension could register anything with the Core.
proof: Real Core, real handler processes: extension registrations are reversible, journaled on the session, rebuilt after restart, and a late answer from an unloaded handler is discarded.
negative_proof: Mutation: removing the liveness re-check lets the stale rewrite land and fails the test.

ci.note: every job green on macOS, Linux and Windows on the rebased head (after IMP-EV-0029 landed); one change carries IMP-EV-0042, 0139 and 0240

limitations: Handlers run as host processes with a scrubbed environment (not sandboxed further, like MCP stdio servers); payloads are summaries; only tool arguments can be rewritten; no signature or marketplace trust on extensions in this change (IMP-EV-0225).
